1032.question_asked:
Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
Hint: league with highest matches of all time refers to MAX(COUNT(league_id));
1032.answer_text: The highest total number of matches recorded is 3,040. This count is shared by three leagues: England Premier League, France Ligue 1, and Spain LIGA BBVA.
1032.executed_sql:
SELECT l.name AS league_name, sub.match_count
FROM (
    SELECT m.league_id, COUNT(*) AS match_count
    FROM cn_e1b70dcdfda248fc.match AS m
    GROUP BY m.league_id
) AS sub
JOIN cn_e1b70dcdfda248fc.league AS l
    ON l.id = sub.league_id
WHERE sub.match_count = (
    SELECT MAX(cnt) FROM (
        SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt

1148.question_asked:
What is the percentage of players that are under 180 cm who have an overall strength of more than 70?
Hint: percentage refers to DIVIDE(COUNT(height < 180 AND overall_rating > 70),COUNT(height < 180)) * 100
1148.answer_text: The percentage of players shorter than 180 cm with an overall rating above 70 is approximately 34.43 %.

SELECT (100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE pa.overall_rating > 70) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0)) AS percentage
FROM cn_e1b70dcdfda248fc.player p
JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (player_api_id) *
    FROM cn_e1b70dcdfda248fc.player_attributes
    ORDER BY player_api_id, date::timestamptz DESC
) pa ON p.player_api_id = pa.player_api_id
WHERE p.height < 180

    WHEN cnt_total = 0 THEN 0

    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (

    WHERE p.height < 180
) sub

  LIMIT 1
)

598.question_asked:
What is the percentage difference of student badges given during 2010 and 2011?
Hint: student badges refers to badge's name = 'Student'; during 2010 refers to Year(Date) = 2010; during 2011 refers to Year(Date) = 2011; percentage difference = Subtract (Divide(Count(Name where Year(Date) = 2010), Count (Name)) *100, Divide(Count(Name where Year(Date) = 2011), Count(Name)) * 100)
598.answer_text: The percentage difference in student badges between 2010 and 2011 is -56.66%.

944.question_asked:
How much faster in percentage is the champion than the driver who finished the race last in the 1988 Australian Grand Prix?
Hint: how much faster in percentage = divide(incremental time, last_driver finished time) * 100; last driver finished time = incremental time + champion time; only champion's finished time is represented by 'HH:MM:SS.mmm'; finished the game refers to time is not null
944.answer_text: The calculated percentage difference is approximately -8,384 %. This negative value indicates that, according to the provided data, the champion’s race time was longer (i.e., slower) than the last‑place driver’s time by about 8,384 %.
944.executed_sql:
WITH selected_race AS (
  SELECT r.raceid
  FROM cn_dbd54b57e3f84128.races r
  WHERE r.year = 1988
    AND r.name = 'Australian Grand Prix'
),
champion AS (
  SELECT extract(epoch FROM res.time::interval) AS champ_sec
  FROM cn_dbd54b57e3f84128.results res
  JOIN selected_race sr ON res.raceid = sr.raceid
  WHERE res.position = 1
    AND res.time IS NOT NULL
),
last_driver AS (
  SELECT extract(epoch FROM res.time::interval) AS last_sec
  FROM cn_dbd54b57e3f84128.results res
  JOIN selected_race sr ON res.raceid = sr.raceid
  WHERE res.time IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY res.position DESC NULLS LAST
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT ((ld.last_sec - ch.champ_sec) / ld.last_sec) * 100 AS percentage_faster
FROM champion ch, last_driver ld

1149.question_asked:
Are there more in-patient or outpatient who were male? What is the deviation in percentage?
Hint: male refers to SEX = 'M'; in-patient refers to Admission = '+'; outpatient refers to Admission = '-'; percentage = DIVIDE(COUNT(ID) where SEX = 'M' and Admission = '+', COUNT(ID) where SEX  = 'M' and Admission = '-')
1149.answer_text: Outpatient males outnumber in‑patient males. The deviation is 83.18 % (outpatient count is 83.18 % higher than the in‑patient count).
1149.executed_sql:
SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN sub.in_cnt > sub.out_cnt THEN 'in-patient'
    WHEN sub.out_cnt > sub.in_cnt THEN 'outpatient'
    ELSE 'equal'
  END AS more_category,
  ROUND((sub.in_cnt::numeric / NULLIF(sub.out_cnt, 0)) * 100, 2) AS deviation_percentage
FROM (
  SELECT 
    COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.sex = 'M' AND p.admission = '+') AS in_cnt,
    COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.sex = 'M' AND p.admission = '-') AS out_cnt
  FROM cn_be782f3725e34f54.patient AS p
) AS sub

1168.question_asked:
For the oldest SJS patient, on what date was their medical laboratory work last completed, and what age was the patient when they initially arrived at the hospital?
Hint: The larger the birthday value, the younger the person is, and vice versa; 'SJS' refers to Patient.Diagnosis; (SUBTRACT(year(`First Date`)), year(Birthday)); age of the patients when they initially arrived at the hospital refers to year(Birthday)
1168.answer_text: The oldest SJS patient had their most recent medical laboratory work completed on 1986-01-07, and they were 69 years old when they first arrived at the hospital.
1168.executed_sql:
WITH oldest AS (
  SELECT p.id, p.birthday, p."First Date"
  FROM cn_be782f3725e34f54.patient p
  WHERE p.diagnosis = 'SJS'
  ORDER BY p.birthday ASC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
  (SELECT MAX(l.date) 
   FROM cn_be782f3725e34f54.laboratory l 
   WHERE l.id = oldest.id) AS last_lab_date,
  (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oldest."First Date") - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM oldest.birthday))::int AS age_at_arrival
FROM oldest

Hint: annual average consumption of customer with the lowest consumption in each segment = total consumption per year / the number of customer with lowest consumption in each segment; Difference in annual average = SME's annual average - LAM's annual average; Difference in annual average = LAM's annual average - KAM's annual average; Year 2013 can be presented as Between 201301 And 201312; The first 4 strings of the Date values in the yearmonth table can represent year.
1481.answer_text:
In 2013, the calculated differences in annual average consumption (CZK) for the customers with the lowest consumption are:
- SME vs LAM: -14,009.34 CZK (SME’s average is lower than LAM’s by about 14,009 CZK).
- LAM vs KAM: 6,046.62 CZK (LAM’s average is higher than KAM’s by about 6,047 CZK).
- KAM vs SME: 7,962.72 CZK (KAM’s average is higher than SME’s by about 7,963 CZK).
1481.executed_sql:
WITH cust_totals AS (
 SELECT c.customerid,
        c.segment,
        SUM(y.consumption) AS total_cons
 FROM cn_dfa531d796da43e7.customers c
 JOIN cn_dfa531d796da43e7.yearmonth y
   ON c.customerid = y.customerid
 WHERE c.currency = 'CZK'
   AND c.segment IN ('SME','LAM','KAM')
   AND y.date LIKE '2013%'
 GROUP BY c.customerid, c.segment
),
seg_min AS (
 SELECT ct.segment,
        MIN(ct.total_cons) AS min_total
 FROM cust_totals ct
 GROUP BY ct.segment
),
seg_avg AS (
 SELECT ct.segment,
        SUM(ct.total_cons) / COUNT(*) AS avg_consumption
 FROM cust_totals ct
 JOIN seg_min sm
   ON ct.segment = sm.segment AND ct.total_cons = sm.min_total
 GROUP BY ct.segment
)
SELECT
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'SME') -
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'LAM') AS diff_sme_lam,
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'LAM') -
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'KAM') AS diff_lam_kam,
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'KAM') -
 (SELECT avg_consumption FROM seg_avg WHERE segment = 'SME') AS diff_kam_sme

1486.question_asked:
Is it true that more SMEs pay in Czech koruna than in euros? If so, how many more?
Hint: Amount of more SMEs = Total of SMEs pay using Currency CZK - Total of SMEs pay using Currency EUR
1486.answer_text: Yes, more SMEs pay in Czech koruna than in euros. The difference is 103,276.44 more SMEs paying with CZK.
1486.executed_sql:
SELECT
    (sub.czk_total > sub.eur_total) AS more_czk,
    sub.czk_total - sub.eur_total AS amount_more
FROM (
    SELECT
        SUM(t.price) FILTER (WHERE c.currency = 'CZK') AS czk_total,
        SUM(t.price) FILTER (WHERE c.currency = 'EUR') AS eur_total
    FROM cn_dfa531d796da43e7.transactions_1k t
    JOIN cn_dfa531d796da43e7.customers c
      ON t.customerid = c.customerid
    WHERE c.segment = 'SME'
) sub

1531.question_asked:
Who is the top spending customer and how much is the average price per single item purchased by this customer? What currency was being used?
Hint: average price per single item = Total(price) / Total(amount)
1531.answer_text: The top‑spending customer is customer ID 19182. For this customer, the average price per single item purchased is 24.28 (CZK). The transactions were recorded in Czech koruna (CZK).
1531.executed_sql:
with cust_tot as (
  select t.customerid,
         sum(t.price) as total_spent,
         sum(t.amount) as total_amount
  from cn_dfa531d796da43e7.transactions_1k t
  group by t.customerid
)
select c.customerid,
       ct.total_spent / nullif(ct.total_amount, 0) as avg_price_per_item,
       c.currency
from cust_tot ct
join cn_dfa531d796da43e7.customers c
  on c.customerid = ct.customerid
order by ct.total_spent desc
limit 1

12.question_asked:
Among the schools with an SAT excellence rate of over 0.3, what is the highest eligible free rate for students aged 5-17?
Hint: Excellence rate = NumGE1500 / NumTstTakr; Eligible free rates for students aged 5-17 = "Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" / "Enrollment (Ages 5-17)"
12.answer_text: The highest eligible free rate for students aged 5-17 among schools with an SAT excellence rate above 0.3 is 0.9049 (or 90.49%).
12.executed_sql:
SELECT MAX(f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)", 0)) AS highest_eligible_free_rate
FROM cn_9240ceb08edb4938.satscores AS s
JOIN cn_9240ceb08edb4938.frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cds
WHERE s."numtsttakr" > 0
  AND s."numge1500" IS NOT NULL

169.question_asked:
What was the growth rate of the total amount of loans across all accounts owned by a male client between 1996 and 1997?
Hint: Growth rate = (sum of amount_1997 - sum of amount_1996) / (sum of amount_1996) * 100%; Male refers to gender = 'M'
169.answer_text: The growth rate of the total loan amount for male clients between 1996 and 1997 was 25.30%.
169.executed_sql:
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN sum_1996 = 0 THEN NULL 
        ELSE ((sum_1997 - sum_1996)::numeric / sum_1996) * 100 
    END AS growth_rate
FROM (
    SELECT
        SUM(CASE 
                WHEN loan.date BETWEEN DATE '1996-01-01' AND DATE '1996-12-31' 
                THEN loan.amount 
                ELSE 0 
            END) AS sum_1996,
        SUM(CASE 
                WHEN loan.date BETWEEN DATE '1997-01-01' AND DATE '1997-12-31' 
                THEN loan.amount 
                ELSE 0 
            END) AS sum_1997
    FROM cn_b7185de16da64408.loan AS loan
    JOIN cn_b7185de16da64408.account AS acc ON acc.account_id = loan.account_id
    JOIN cn_b7185de16da64408.disp AS d ON d.account_id = acc.account_id AND d.type = 'OWNER'
    JOIN cn_b7185de16da64408.client AS c ON c.client_id = d.client_id
    WHERE c.gender = 'M'
) sub

1150.question_asked:

Hint: female refers to Sex = 'F'; patient who were born after 1930 refers to year(Birthday) > '1930'; calculation = DIVIDE(COUNT(ID) where year(Birthday) > '1930' and SEX = 'F'), (COUNT(ID) where SEX = 'F')
1150.answer_text: The proportion of female patients born after 1930 is 94.04% (approximately).
1150.executed_sql:
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN sub.total_female = 0 THEN 0
        ELSE (sub.filtered_female * 100.0) / sub.total_female

FROM (
    SELECT 
        COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.sex = 'F') AS total_female,
        COUNT(p.id) FILTER (WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND p.birthday::timestamptz > TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE '1930-12-31 00:00:00+00') AS filtered_female
    FROM cn_be782f3725e34f54.patient p

FROM cn_dfa531d796da43e7.yearmonth AS ym
JOIN (
    SELECT DISTINCT t.customerid
    FROM cn_dfa531d796da43e7.transactions_1k AS t
    WHERE t.productid = 5
      AND (t.price / t.amount) > 29.00
) AS filtered ON filtered.customerid = ym.customerid
WHERE ym.date = '201208'
